samples.xml_description:
Implement an asynchronous FIFO, FIFO bit width and depth can be configured(parameter DEPTH = 16, parameter WIDTH = 8). The asynchronous FIFO structure is divided into several parts. The first part is dual-port RAM, which is used for data storage. Instantiate dual-port RAM as a submodule, The RAM ports are input wclk, input wenc, input [$clog2(DEPTH)-1:0] waddr, input [WIDTH-1:0] wdata, input rclk, input renc, input [$clog2(DEPTH)-1:0] raddr, output reg [WIDTH-1:0] rdata. The second part is the data write controller. The third part is the data read controller. The fourth part is the read pointer synchronizer. The read pointer is collected using the two-stage trigger of the write clock and output to the data write controller. The fifth part is the write pointer synchronizer, which uses the two-stage trigger of the read clock to collect the write pointer and output it to the data read controller. Write clock signal used for synchronous write operations. Read clock signal used for synchronous read operations. Write reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive. Read reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive. Write increment signal. Used to trigger write operations. Read increment signal. Used to trigger read operations. Write data input. The width [WIDTH-1:0] is configurable and represents the data to be written into the FIFO. Write full signal. Indicates if the FIFO is full and cannot accept further write operations. Read empty signal. Indicates if the FIFO is empty and cannot provide any data for read operations. Read data output. The width [WIDTH-1:0] is configurable and represents the data read from the FIFO. 8. Internal parameter. 16. Internal parameter. 4. Internal parameter. reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] raddr_bin; sequential logic, executes when positive edge of rclk or negative edge of rrstn. raddr_bin size is (ADDR_WIDTH + 1) bits. If rrstn is deactive, raddr_bin is all zero. Otherwise, raddr_bin is incremented by 1 if rempty is deactive and rinc is active. reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] raddr_gray; combinational logic. raddr_gray is XOR operation between raddr_bin and shift-left-1 operation of raddr_bin. reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rptr; sequential logic, executes when positive edge of rclk or negative edge of rrstn. rptr size is (ADDR_WIDTH + 1) bits. If wrstn is deactive, rptr is all zero. Otherwise, rptr is set to raddr_gray. reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rptr_buff; sequential logic, executes when positive edge of wclk or negative edge of wrstn. rptr_buff size is (ADDR_WIDTH + 1) bits. If wrstn is deactive, rptr_buff is all zero. Otherwise, rptr_buff is set to rptr. reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] rptr_syn; sequential logic, executes when positive edge of wclk or negative edge of wrstn. rptr_syn size is (ADDR_WIDTH + 1) bits. If wrstn is deactive, rptr_syn is all zero. Otherwise, rptr_syn is set to rptr_buff. reg ren; combinational logic. Internal read enable logic. ren is active if rinc is active and rempty is deactive. reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] waddr_bin; sequential logic, executes when positive edge of wclk or negative edge of wrstn. waddr_bin size is (ADDR_WIDTH + 1) bits. If wrstn is deactive, waddr_bin is all zero. Otherwise, waddr_bin is incremented by 1 if wfull is deactive and winc is active. reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] waddr_gray; combinational logic. waddr_gray is XOR operation between waddr_bin and shift-left-1 operation of waddr_bin. reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wptr; sequential logic, executes when positive edge of wclk or negative edge of wrstn. wptr size is (ADDR_WIDTH + 1) bits. If wrstn is deactive, wptr is all zero. Otherwise, wptr is set to waddr_gray. reg wfull; combinational logic. The wfull output is set to 1 when the wptr is equal to the bitwise negation of the 2 most significant bits of the rptr_syn concatenated with the remaining bits of the rptr_syn. reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wptr_buff; sequential logic, executes when positive edge of rclk or negative edge of rrstn. wptr_buff size is (ADDR_WIDTH + 1) bits. If rrstn is deactive, wptr_buff is all zero. Otherwise, wptr_buff is set to wptr. reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wptr_syn; sequential logic, executes when positive edge of rclk or negative edge of rrstn. wptr_syn size is (ADDR_WIDTH + 1) bits. If rrstn is deactive, wptr_syn is all zero. Otherwise, wptr_syn is set to wptr_buff. reg wen; combinational logic. Internal write enable logic. wen is active if winc is active and wfull is deactive. reg rempty; combinational logic. rempty is active if rptr is equaled to wptr_syn.

Asynchronous FIFO is implemented using dual-port RAM module and additional logic for managing read and write pointers.

Dual-port RAM:

The module instantiates a dual-port RAM module named "dual_port_RAM" with configurable depth and width.

The RAM module has separate clock inputs for write (wclk) and read (rclk) operations.

The RAM module has separate address inputs for write (waddr) and read (raddr) operations.

The RAM module has a write enable input (wenc) and a write data input (wdata).

The RAM module has a read enable input (renc) and a read data output (rdata).

The RAM module stores data in a two-dimensional array, RAM_MEM, with a size of DEPTH by WIDTH.

The following logics from the top module asyn_fifo are used to instantiates the dual_port_RAM: wclk, wen, waddr, wdata, rclk, ren, raddr, rdata:

  • wclk to wclk of asyn_fifo.
  • wenc to wen of asyn_fifo.
  • waddr to waddr of asyn_fifo.
  • wdata to wdata of asyn_fifo.
  • rclk to rclk of asyn_fifo.
  • renc to ren of asyn_fifo.
  • raddr to raddr of asyn_fifo.
  • rdata to rdata of asyn_fifo.

Write and Read Pointers:

The module includes logic to manage write and read pointers for asynchronous operation.

The write and read pointers are represented by binary registers, waddr_bin and raddr_bin, respectively.
